settings.slogan: Quality Defects & Root Cause Knowledge Platform

categories.name: Crimping
categories.description: Terminal crimping defects on automatic and benchtop crimping presses (Komax / Schleuniger). Detected by crimp-force monitoring (CFA) and cross-section (micrograph) analysis

categories.name: Seal
categories.description: Single-wire seal (grommet) defects on seal-crimp modules — sealing integrity for sealed connector cavities and seal pull-force requirements.

categories.name: Stripping
categories.description: Cut & strip defects on automatic cut/strip machines (Komax / Schleuniger) — conductor and insulation quality

failureTypes.name: Strands out of the crimp
failureTypes.description: One or more conductor strands are not enclosed by the wire barrel and lie outside the crimp.

failureTypes.name: Strands on the crimp
failureTypes.description: Loose strands (whiskers) lie on top of the insulation crimp or between the wire and insulation barrels, risking shorts.

failureTypes.name: Crimp height out of specification
failureTypes.description: Measured conductor crimp height is outside the tolerance band, affecting mechanical and electrical integrity.

failureTypes.name: Bellmouth non-conform
failureTypes.description: The flare (bellmouth) at the wire-barrel ends is missing, too small, or excessive at the front or rear.

failureTypes.name: Insufficient conductor brush
failureTypes.description: The conductor brush (strands visible beyond the wire barrel) is too short or not visible, per IPC/WHMA-A-620.

failureTypes.name: Insulation in the conductor crimp
failureTypes.description: Insulation is caught inside the wire (conductor) barrel, reducing electrical contact and pull force.

failureTypes.name: Insulation crimp grip out of tolerance
failureTypes.description: The insulation (support) crimp is too loose (no strain relief) or too tight (cuts the insulation).

failureTypes.name: Terminal deformation
failureTypes.description: The terminal is bent, twisted, rolled, or the contact / box section is deformed after crimping.

failureTypes.name: Crimp force curve out of tolerance
failureTypes.description: The crimp-force monitor (Komax ACO / Schleuniger CFA) flags the crimp-force curve outside the taught envelope.

failureTypes.name: Missing seal
failureTypes.description: No single-wire seal is present on the wire before the seal crimp.

failureTypes.name: Seal damaged
failureTypes.description: The seal is cut, torn, or nicked, compromising the sealing lips.

failureTypes.name: Seal position out of tolerance
failureTypes.description: The seal sits too far forward or back on the wire relative to the terminal.

failureTypes.name: Seal deformed by crimp
failureTypes.description: The elastic seal is severely deformed by the insulation / seal crimp, impairing sealing and pull force.

failureTypes.name: Wrong seal type or size
failureTypes.description: A seal of the wrong colour / size / part number is fitted for the wire cross-section.

failureTypes.name: Seal not fully seated on the wire
failureTypes.description: The seal is only partially pushed onto the wire; it can move or leak.

failureTypes.name: Double seal or seal skew
failureTypes.description: Two seals are loaded, or the seal is cocked / skewed on the wire.

failureTypes.name: Strands cut or nicked
failureTypes.description: Conductor strands are nicked or fully cut during stripping — a defect for all classes when the conductor is damaged, per IPC/WHMA-A-620.

failureTypes.name: Insulation residue on conductor
failureTypes.description: Slivers or rings of insulation remain on the conductor after stripping.

failureTypes.name: Strip length out of specification
failureTypes.description: The stripped length is outside the tolerance for the downstream crimp or seal.

failureTypes.name: Incomplete insulation removal
failureTypes.description: The insulation is only partly cut or removed, so the slug hangs on or the strip is partial.

failureTypes.name: Conductor deformed or flattened
failureTypes.description: The conductor is pinched, flattened, or strands are distorted by the strip clamps or blades.

failureTypes.name: Insulation not removed
failureTypes.description: The wire end is cut, but the insulation is not stripped at all.

failureTypes.name: Cut length out of tolerance
failureTypes.description: The overall wire cut length is outside tolerance.

failureTypes.name: Ragged or torn insulation cut
failureTypes.description: The insulation cut edge is ragged, torn, or stretched rather than clean.

failureTypes.name: Conductor ring-cut (score) on strands
failureTypes.description: A visible ring score around the conductor from blade over-penetration, creating a stress riser.

rootCauses.title: Swivel arm / wire guide position not well defined
rootCauses.description: The wire-transfer swivel arm or guide feeds the conductor off-centre into the applicator, so strands fall outside the wire barrel.

steps.instruction: Reset the swivel arm / wire guide to the reference position on the applicator setup sheet.
Run three test crimps and cross-section one to confirm all strands are enclosed.
Confirm no loose strands are visible outside the wire barrel under magnification.

rootCauses.title: Conductor brush splays after stripping (birdcage)
rootCauses.description: Strands splay open (birdcage) after stripping and spread beyond the barrel during insertion.

steps.instruction: Reduce the stripping blade opening or add a strand-align / straightener device.
Enable wire-end detection and re-run the transfer.
Verify strands stay bundled at the moment of insertion.

rootCauses.title: Terminal not centred in the applicator
rootCauses.description: The terminal is off-centre on the anvil, shifting the barrel away from the conductor.

steps.instruction: Centre the terminal track and anvil to the applicator centreline.
Perform a test crimp and inspect strand capture.
Check terminal centring on the anvil under magnification.

rootCauses.title: Strip length too short for the wire barrel
rootCauses.description: The stripped conductor is shorter than the wire barrel, so the last strands are not gripped.

steps.instruction: Increase strip length to match the barrel per the crimp specification.
Re-measure conductor brush and barrel coverage.
Confirm the conductor fills the full length of the wire barrel.

rootCauses.title: Strip length too long
rootCauses.description: Excess bared conductor reaches into the insulation crimp zone, leaving strands on top of the crimp.

steps.instruction: Reduce strip length to the crimp specification.
Verify the brush transition between conductor and insulation crimp.
Confirm no strands lie over the insulation barrel.

rootCauses.title: Stray strands from damaged stripping blades
rootCauses.description: Worn stripping blades shear individual strands that then lie on the crimp.

steps.instruction: Inspect and replace the stripping blades.
Clean the strip station and re-run.
Verify the strand count is complete and no stray strands remain.

rootCauses.title: Poor wire transfer alignment
rootCauses.description: The conductor is presented off-axis, so stray strands fold onto the crimp.

steps.instruction: Re-align the gripper / transfer to the applicator.
Test-crimp and inspect.
Check the conductor sits central before crimping.

rootCauses.title: Applicator wear / beyond maintenance interval
rootCauses.description: A worn applicator produces progressively shallow or inconsistent crimp heights across a run.

steps.instruction: Replace or service the applicator crimp tooling per the maintenance schedule.
Recalibrate crimp height to the spec sheet and log the reading.
Measure crimp height on 5 pieces and confirm all are within tolerance.

rootCauses.title: Wrong shut height / press setup
rootCauses.description: The press shut height is set incorrectly for the terminal, giving over- or under-compression.

steps.instruction: Set the press shut height to the applicator reference value.
Run a crimp-height and pull-force check.
Confirm crimp height and pull force meet the spec.

rootCauses.title: Wrong terminal or wire size for the applicator
rootCauses.description: A terminal/wire combination outside the applicator range yields out-of-spec height.

steps.instruction: Verify the terminal part number and wire cross-section against the crimp chart.
Load the correct applicator / wire and re-test.
Confirm terminal PN and wire CSA match the crimp chart.

rootCauses.title: Crimp-force monitor not taught or disabled
rootCauses.description: The CFM reference (ACO / CFA) is not taught, so height drift is not caught.

steps.instruction: Re-teach the crimp-force reference on verified good samples.
Enable automatic reject for out-of-band curves.
Confirm the crimp-force monitor is active and the envelope is taught.

rootCauses.title: Worn or damaged crimp tooling
rootCauses.description: Worn anvil / crimper edges fail to form a proper bellmouth.

steps.instruction: Inspect the anvil and crimper radius; replace if worn.
Test-crimp and inspect front and rear bellmouth.
Confirm a symmetric bellmouth is present at both barrel ends.

rootCauses.title: Incorrect conductor positioning in the barrel
rootCauses.description: The conductor set too far forward or back changes bellmouth formation.

steps.instruction: Adjust the wire stop / conductor position in the barrel.
Re-crimp and inspect.
Confirm brush and bellmouth are within the inspection window.

rootCauses.title: Crimp height too high (under-compression)
rootCauses.description: Under-compression leaves an oversized or irregular bellmouth.

steps.instruction: Correct crimp height to spec.
Re-inspect the bellmouth form.
Confirm bellmouth size is within acceptance criteria.

rootCauses.title: Strip length too short
rootCauses.description: Too little conductor is exposed, so no brush is visible beyond the barrel.

steps.instruction: Increase strip length so the brush is visible beyond the wire barrel.
Re-measure brush length.
Confirm the brush is visible and within min/max.

rootCauses.title: Wire set too far into the barrel
rootCauses.description: The conductor is inserted too deep, hiding the brush inside the barrel.

steps.instruction: Adjust the wire stop so the conductor extends past the barrel.
Test-crimp and inspect.
Confirm the conductor extends beyond the wire barrel.

rootCauses.title: Strip length too short
rootCauses.description: Insulation reaches into the conductor barrel because too little was stripped.

steps.instruction: Increase strip length to clear insulation from the wire barrel.
Re-crimp and cross-section to verify.
Confirm no insulation inside the conductor barrel.

rootCauses.title: Insulation not fully removed at strip
rootCauses.description: A residual insulation slug is carried into the crimp.

steps.instruction: Correct blade depth / position to fully remove the insulation slug.
Verify clean conductor at the strip station.
Confirm the conductor is clean before crimp.

rootCauses.title: Wire positioned too far back
rootCauses.description: The wire stop leaves insulation inside the conductor barrel.

steps.instruction: Adjust the wire stop / transfer so insulation stays in the insulation barrel.
Re-test.
Confirm insulation sits only in the insulation crimp.

rootCauses.title: Wrong insulation crimp height / tooling
rootCauses.description: The insulation crimp height does not match the wire outer diameter.

steps.instruction: Set the insulation crimp height for the wire OD per spec.
Verify grip with a wiggle / pull check.
Confirm insulation is held without cutting through.

media.caption: Insulation crimp grip out of tolerance

rootCauses.title: Wire outer diameter out of range
rootCauses.description: The wire OD is outside the applicator window, so grip is loose or over-tight.

steps.instruction: Verify wire OD / insulation against the applicator range.
Select the correct applicator or insulation crimp setting.
Confirm wire OD within the applicator window.

media.caption: Insulation crimp grip out of tolerance

rootCauses.title: Terminal feed / carrier not correctly aligned
rootCauses.description: Misaligned feed or cut-off distorts the terminal during crimp.

steps.instruction: Align the terminal feed and cut-off to the applicator.
Inspect the box / contact section after crimp.
Confirm the contact section is straight and undamaged.

rootCauses.title: Excessive crimp force / wrong shut height
rootCauses.description: Over-compression deforms the contact area.

steps.instruction: Correct shut height and crimp force to spec.
Re-crimp and inspect for deformation.
Confirm no deformation of the contact area.

rootCauses.title: Cut-off tab burr pushing the terminal
rootCauses.description: A burr on the carrier cut-off tab pushes and bends the terminal.

steps.instruction: Adjust the cut-off blade to remove the burr and correct tab length.
Inspect the terminal after cut-off.
Confirm cut-off tab length and no burr.

rootCauses.title: Missing strands / short brush
rootCauses.description: Fewer strands or a short brush lower the crimp force below the envelope.

steps.instruction: Check upstream stripping for cut or missing strands.
Correct the strip and re-teach if needed.
Confirm the full strand count enters the barrel.

media.caption: Crimp force curve out of tolerance

rootCauses.title: Terminal or wire material variation
rootCauses.description: A new terminal or wire lot shifts the force curve out of the taught band.

steps.instruction: Verify the terminal lot and wire; re-teach the CFM reference on the new lot.
Confirm the curve returns within envelope.
Confirm the CFM curve is inside the taught band.

media.caption: Crimp force curve out of tolerance

rootCauses.title: Reference envelope taught on bad samples
rootCauses.description: The CFM was taught on defective crimps, so the envelope is invalid.

steps.instruction: Re-teach the CFM using verified good crimps (cross-sectioned).
Validate with known-good and known-bad pieces.
Confirm good pieces pass and defects are rejected.

media.caption: Crimp force curve out of tolerance

rootCauses.title: Seal feeder empty or jammed
rootCauses.description: The seal feeder (bowl / tape) is empty or jammed, so no seal is loaded.

steps.instruction: Refill or clear the seal feeder and re-home the module.
Run a test cycle and confirm seal pick-up.
Confirm a seal is present on every wire.

rootCauses.title: Seal-presence sensor disabled or misaligned
rootCauses.description: The seal detection sensor is off or misaligned, so no-seal parts pass.

steps.instruction: Enable and align the seal-presence sensor.
Verify it rejects a deliberately no-seal part.
Confirm the sensor detects a missing seal.

rootCauses.title: Worn or sharp seal transfer tooling
rootCauses.description: Worn seal-loading fingers or tooling cut the seal body during handling.

steps.instruction: Inspect and replace the seal-loading fingers / tooling.
Run test pieces and inspect the seal body.
Confirm the seal lips are intact and undamaged.

rootCauses.title: Seal crimp height too tight
rootCauses.description: An over-tight seal crimp cuts or tears the elastic seal.

steps.instruction: Increase the seal crimp height to the spec.
Inspect for cuts after crimp.
Confirm no cuts or tears on the seal.

rootCauses.title: Wire strand pierces the seal during insertion
rootCauses.description: A splayed strand punctures the seal bore as the wire is inserted.

steps.instruction: Improve conductor alignment / add a lead-in; check for splayed strands.
Re-run and inspect the seal bore.
Confirm the seal bore is not pierced.

rootCauses.title: Seal stop / positioning incorrectly set
rootCauses.description: The seal position stop is set to the wrong dimension.

steps.instruction: Set the seal position stop to the spec dimension.
Measure seal-to-terminal distance on test pieces.
Confirm the seal position is within tolerance.

rootCauses.title: Strip / cut length variation upstream
rootCauses.description: Inconsistent cut or strip length shifts the seal position.

steps.instruction: Verify cut and strip lengths feeding the seal module.
Correct and re-measure the seal position.
Confirm consistent seal position across samples.

rootCauses.title: Seal crimp height too low (over-crimped)
rootCauses.description: Excessive compression permanently deforms the seal.

steps.instruction: Raise the seal crimp height to the specified value.
Re-crimp and check seal geometry and pull force.
Confirm the seal returns to shape and meets pull force.

rootCauses.title: Wrong seal size for the wire
rootCauses.description: A seal too small for the wire is crushed during crimp.

steps.instruction: Verify the seal PN / size against the wire OD.
Load the correct seal and re-test.
Confirm the seal PN matches the wire.

rootCauses.title: Wrong seal loaded in the feeder
rootCauses.description: The feeder was loaded with a seal that does not match the work order.

steps.instruction: Verify the seal part number against the work order.
Reload the correct seal and purge wrong parts.
Confirm the seal PN and colour match the spec.

rootCauses.title: Insufficient seal insertion stroke
rootCauses.description: The insertion stroke / force does not fully seat the seal.

steps.instruction: Adjust the seal insertion stroke / force to fully seat the seal.
Verify seal seating on test pieces.
Confirm the seal is fully seated against the reference.

media.caption: Seal not fully seated on the wire

rootCauses.title: Wire OD too large / seal bore too small
rootCauses.description: Incompatible wire OD and seal bore prevent full seating.

steps.instruction: Verify wire OD and seal bore compatibility.
Select the correct seal.
Confirm the seal slides on and seats without a gap.

media.caption: Seal not fully seated on the wire

rootCauses.title: Feeder singulation fault
rootCauses.description: The seal escapement / singulation picks two seals or presents one skewed.

steps.instruction: Service the seal singulation / escapement in the feeder.
Run test cycles to confirm a single-seal pick.
Confirm exactly one seal per wire, square to the axis.

rootCauses.title: Stripping blade depth set too deep
rootCauses.description: The blade cuts into the conductor because the depth of cut is set too deep.

steps.instruction: Reduce the blade cutting depth to just clear the insulation.
Cross-check with a strand-contact detection (e.g. SmartDetect) run.
Confirm no nicked or cut strands under magnification.

rootCauses.title: Worn or damaged stripping blades
rootCauses.description: Dull or chipped blades tear or nick strands instead of cleanly cutting insulation.

steps.instruction: Replace the stripping blades and clean the station.
Run test pieces and inspect strands.
Confirm the full strand count with no damage.

rootCauses.title: Blade not centred on the wire (off-axis)
rootCauses.description: A wire off the blade axis is nicked on one side.

steps.instruction: Centre the blades to the wire axis / correct the V-blade alignment.
Re-strip and inspect.
Confirm a concentric strip with no one-sided nicking.

rootCauses.title: Wrong blade type for the conductor
rootCauses.description: A blade profile unsuited to fine-strand or thin-wall wire damages strands.

steps.instruction: Fit the correct blade geometry for the wire (e.g. fine-strand or thin-wall).
Validate on samples.
Confirm the blade type matches the wire spec.

rootCauses.title: Blade depth too shallow
rootCauses.description: The blade does not fully sever the insulation, leaving residue.

steps.instruction: Increase the blade depth to fully sever the insulation.
Re-strip and inspect for residue.
Confirm the conductor is clean of insulation.

rootCauses.title: Pull-off distance too short / slug not removed
rootCauses.description: The strip stroke does not fully pull the insulation slug off.

steps.instruction: Increase the pull-off (strip) stroke to fully remove the slug.
Verify complete slug removal.
Confirm no insulation ring at the strip transition.

rootCauses.title: Blunt blades on tough insulation
rootCauses.description: Cross-linked or tough insulation is not cleanly cut by worn blades.

steps.instruction: Replace blades; adjust settings for the insulation material.
Re-test.
Confirm a clean cut on the insulation.

rootCauses.title: Strip length parameter incorrect
rootCauses.description: The programmed strip length does not match the crimp / seal spec.

steps.instruction: Set the strip length parameter to the crimp / seal spec.
Measure strip length on test pieces.
Confirm strip length within tolerance.

rootCauses.title: Wire slip in the belts / clamps
rootCauses.description: Wire slipping in the feed belts or clamps causes length drift.

steps.instruction: Check and adjust belt / clamp pressure to prevent slip.
Re-measure over several pieces.
Confirm consistent strip length (no drift).

rootCauses.title: Encoder / length calibration off
rootCauses.description: The length measurement (encoder / roller) is out of calibration.

steps.instruction: Recalibrate the length measurement (encoder / roller).
Validate against a measured reference.
Confirm measured vs programmed length match.

rootCauses.title: Clamp / cut timing not synchronised
rootCauses.description: The cutter moves before the wire is fully clamped, giving a partial strip.

steps.instruction: Correct the clamp-then-cut timing so the wire is held before cutting.
Re-run and inspect.
Confirm full clean removal every cycle.

rootCauses.title: Insufficient cut depth
rootCauses.description: The insulation is not fully severed, so the slug stays attached.

steps.instruction: Increase cut depth to fully sever the insulation.
Verify complete removal.
Confirm no partial slug remains.

rootCauses.title: Clamp force too high
rootCauses.description: Excess gripper / clamp force flattens the conductor.

steps.instruction: Reduce clamp / gripper force to hold without deforming.
Inspect conductor shape.
Confirm a round, undamaged conductor.

rootCauses.title: Blades closing onto the conductor
rootCauses.description: The blades close too far at pull-off and squeeze the conductor.

steps.instruction: Increase the blade opening at pull-off to clear the conductor.
Re-strip and inspect.
Confirm the blades do not contact the conductor.

rootCauses.title: Blades not closing / stripping disabled
rootCauses.description: The strip head does not actuate or the recipe has stripping disabled.

steps.instruction: Verify the strip head actuates and the recipe enables stripping.
Run a test cycle.
Confirm insulation is removed on every end.

rootCauses.title: Wire mis-fed / not clamped
rootCauses.description: The wire slips or is not clamped, so the strip head misses it.

steps.instruction: Check the wire feed and clamp; clear any slip or jam.
Re-run.
Confirm the wire is clamped before strip.

rootCauses.title: Length calibration / material stretch
rootCauses.description: Miscalibration or wire stretch produces the wrong cut length.

steps.instruction: Recalibrate cut length; compensate for wire stretch / slip.
Measure several pieces.
Confirm cut length within tolerance.

rootCauses.title: Belt / roller wear or slip
rootCauses.description: Worn feed belts or rollers cause length variation.

steps.instruction: Inspect and replace worn feed belts / rollers.
Re-verify length.
Confirm stable length across a run.

rootCauses.title: Dull blades
rootCauses.description: Worn blades tear rather than cleanly cut the insulation.

steps.instruction: Replace the stripping blades.
Inspect the cut-edge quality.
Confirm a clean, square insulation cut.

rootCauses.title: Strip speed too high for the material
rootCauses.description: A high pull-off speed tears elastic or soft insulation.

steps.instruction: Reduce the pull-off speed for elastic / soft insulation.
Re-test.
Confirm no tearing or stretching.

rootCauses.title: Blade depth slightly over the conductor
rootCauses.description: The blade lightly scores the strands around the full circumference.

steps.instruction: Back off the blade depth to the insulation-only setting.
Use strand-contact detection to confirm.
Confirm no ring score on the conductor.
